messages:
PagerDuty: Incident alert: hosted-api request queue length (us-west-2) exceeded threshold (queue=9.3k, growth rate +1200/min). Possible GPU capacity exhaustion. Pager: P0.

OpsBot: Automated detection: p95 latency spike -> 2.4s (baseline 160ms), p99 -> 8.7s, 504 rate rising. Autoscaler attempted 3 scale-ups; 2 failed due to provider quota errors. Logs: `CreateInstance: QUOTA_EXCEEDED` on batch provisioning. Link: https://dashboards.redwood.internal/queues/us-west-2 (graph attached).

Maya (oncall-eng): oncall here. Confirming impact: Hosted API calls in us-west-2 seeing backlog/timeouts. Customers reporting timeouts and increased latency. Triage steps: 1) identify whether autoscaler failures are transient quota or internal; 2) apply mitigations (fallback routing, admission control, rate-limits); 3) notify support and exec. @Ashwin can you take infra lead?

Ashwin (infra): looking. Autoscaler logs show hit to cloud project vCPU/GPU quota for GPU-accelerator family. Cloud side is returning 429/Quota. Our retry path gives up after 3 attempts because the provisioning call returns PERMANENT_QUOTA in body. Might be a regional quota exhaustion (partner tenant used burst).

Jordan (runtime): meanwhile requests piling up on hosted queue router. We have two low-effort mitigations we can flip quickly: 1) enable model-variant fallback: route sessions to a smaller quantized model (cpu or small-gpu) if primary pool unavailable; 2) enable 'shed-low-priority' admission control to drop or 429 best-effort jobs (non-PLG/test). Both are feature flags we can toggle per-region.

Maya (oncall-eng): do it. Prioritize keeping higher-SLA customers live.

Jordan (runtime): doing now. Flipping flags: `rbac:feature/variant-fallback=on` and `admission:uswest-shed-low=on`

Jordan (runtime): fallback enabled. Routing ~18% of traffic to quantized-smaller models; shed policy rejecting ~12% of low-priority queued requests (we return structured 429 with retry-after).

Leah (support): can someone paste customer impact numbers? I have a message batch ready for affected customers once we know which tenants are impacted (enterprise vs free). Need list for comms ops.

Maya (oncall-eng): from logs: top affected tenants by requests in last 10m: tenant-alpha (20% of errors), tenant-beta (14%), tenant-gamma (8%). We'll flag enterprise-tier for priority routing.

Ashwin (infra): attempted manual scale up via cli. Command: 
```
redwood infra pools scale --region us-west-2 --pool hosted-gpu --add 8 --type a100-80
```
Cloud returned error: `PERMANENT_QUOTA_EXCEEDED: cannot allocate GPUs in region`. I opened a ticket with cloud quota team and submitted emergency quota increase request (ticket #CLOUD-98764). ETA unknown.

Rafael (sre): while cloud quota is pending, we should isolate noisy tenants that caused burst. We have scripts to throttle by API key. Suggest temp restrict tenant-alpha to 25rps and route enterprise keys to dedicated pool (if they have dedicated capacity).

Jordan (runtime): already routed enterprise keys to dedicated-durable pool. Implementing tenant throttles now.

Jordan (runtime): throttle applied to tenant-alpha and tenant-beta. Observed immediate drop in queue growth rate from +1200/min to +300/min. p95 down slightly to 1.1s.

Product NOC: Noted that some partner integration produced a fanout of short requests. Will contact partner ops to ask for traffic smoothing.

Maya (oncall-eng): good. Two parallel tracks: infra pursues quota/rescue provisioning; runtime keeps fallback/admission in place and continues draining queue; support prepares customer comms. Who owns postmortem?

Ashwin (infra): I will continue to chase cloud quota. Filed contact with partner rep for emergency bump. Also creating temporary pool out of other zones (us-west-1) and will enable cross-region routing for low-latency-tolerant workloads.

Jordan (runtime): enabling cross-region route for best-effort jobs: `rbctl route set --region us-west-2 --fallback-region us-west-1 --policy best-effort`

OpsBot: Cross-region fallback enabled. Note: latency for those will increase due to network hop ~60-120ms.

Leah (support): drafting customer note: "We are experiencing elevated latency and intermittent timeouts in US-West. We have applied temporary mitigations (traffic prioritization and fallback routing). Enterprise customers are routed to dedicated capacity. We will update in 30m." Requesting list of tenants moved to dedicated pool.

Maya (oncall-eng): tenant-alpha and tenant-beta are still partially affected; tenant-gamma mostly recovered.

Ashwin (infra): cloud responded: emergency quota ticket escalated to SOC; provisional increase granted for 4 GPUs in us-west-2 for 20 minutes while they review. I will attempt a targeted manual add for burst capacity.

Ashwin (infra): executing scale command for 4 GPUs: `redwood infra pools add --region us-west-2 --pool hosted-gpu --count 4 --type a100-80`

OpsBot: Provisioning request accepted; VMs booting. Provisioner logs: attaching images -> ok; 2/4 instances available. Autoscaler health check: partial success.

Jordan (runtime): as new instances come up we see queue draining. Queue peaked at ~14.1k earlier, now down to 4.2k and dropping. p95 now 420ms, p99 1.1s. 504 rate trending down.

Maya (oncall-eng): excellent. Keep fallback & shed policies for another hour while we verify stability.

Leah (support): sending customer message now. Patch note: affected customers will receive a follow-up with root cause and ETA for full restore.

Rafael (sre): quick note for timeline: detection 3767890000, mitigations applied (fallback+shed) at 3767890300, tenant throttles 3767890600, manual scale partial success 3767891200, queue drained under 1k by 3767891600.

Maya (oncall-eng): moving to handoff. I'll prepare incident doc and postmortem draft. Action items: 
- Infra: add autoscaler retry/backoff for PERMANENT_QUOTA to fallback to alternate zones and to delay giving up so human ops can intervene.
- Runtime: make fallback variant automatic for sustained queue growth > X and include graceful degradation messages to SDK.
- Product: partner contact to enforce rate limits and back-off.
- Support: customer comms template and SLA credits review.

Ashwin (infra): also add monitoring alert for cloud quota exhausted (different severity than provisioning failure) and runbook entry to request emergency quota with template.

Jordan (runtime): opening a follow-up engineering ticket to reduce dependency on single-region GPU quotas for hosted traffic (design proposals: pool bursting across regions, preemptible fallback, CPU-mode for small requests).

Maya (oncall-eng): handing off to Rafael (sre) for overnight. Please watch for recurrence; keep fallbacks until quotas are stable.

Rafael (sre): acknowledged. Handoff received. Will monitor next 6h and reopen if queue growth > 1k/min.

Maya (oncall-eng): incident status -> mitigated. Will mark P0 -> P1 in 30m when stable. Postmortem owner: Ashwin + Jordan.

Leah (support): adding customer follow-ups to CRM and staging post-incident email.

OpsBot: Incident ticket updated: INC-2026-327. Attach logs and runbook link: https://runbooks.redwood.internal/incidents/gpu-queue-backlog.

Maya (oncall-eng): thanks team. Final note: do not remove tenant throttles until Ashwin confirms quota bump is permanent. Handoff complete. :white_check_mark:
